title: A scorched wasteland
paragraphs: "The plot goes like this: Princess Melty secretly performs music, and with Sakura of Filolial as her partner, they spread the word through song to protect Melromarc, Siltvelt, Shieldfreeden—and ultimately the entire world—from the waves engulfing the world and the remnants of the evil pseudo-hero Takt… and is spreading word of this crisis through her songs…”
“Well, well… it seems the Queen of Melromarc has a truly reliable successor.”
The elders of the Shusaku and Genmu clans both offered the Queen their customary words of praise.

“Well then, our nation cannot afford to lag behind forever. I earnestly request that you, the Shield Hero, along with Knight Larsazusa and the other Guardian Knights, do your utmost. It’s about time we increased our ranks as well.”
“Y-yeah, you’re right.”
I heard this later from Father: apparently, he seized this opportunity to imply a request for us to have children behind those words. Even I found that one hard to pick up on.
“In that regard, as a future task—and since Faubrey has also made a request—I’d like to coordinate our efforts regarding the protection of the Sword Hero.”

It seems the Queen has shifted from a lighthearted topic to a serious one. Is this about Ren’s protection? Come to think of it, I haven’t seen him since returning to this loop. Last time, he was erased by Takt, so it feels like it’s been quite a while since I last saw him.

“Due to the blunder committed by our nation, Melromarc, we’ve lost the trust of others, and the whereabouts of the Sword Hero remain unknown. Based on the Spear Hero’s testimony, we’ve requested that Zeltoble conduct a search there as well, and searches are currently underway in various nations, but he has not yet been found.”

All eyes turned to me. So Ren still hasn’t been found, huh? In the loop where we stayed in Melromarc, he would’ve slipped back in under the guise of a righteous hero, taking advantage of the commotion when the queen returned.
“Hasn’t he shown up yet?”

Just how distrustful of people is she? Well, perhaps it’s partly because we weren’t torn to shreds by Trash during the first wave we participated in back then. Ren has a tendency to be unnecessarily stubborn, after all. Objectively speaking, being told to keep your distance might feel different from being told to your face that you’re not trying hard enough.
“Yes… I had intended to have the country’s shadow forces search as well, but since the Hero can teleport…”

When the Portal skill is used, even the Shadow finds it difficult to track him. If I recall correctly, I heard that in the first world—and especially as we began using portals for travel across various loops—the Shadow often ended up confined to monitoring our bases.
“I hope we can find him somewhere and have a talk…”
“Well, I think the Sword Hero of this loop would at least be willing to listen to what we have to say.”
Our Rival seizes the moment and raises his hand to speak.
“Gaelion is trying to lure out the Sword Hero here… no, wait—he might already be here, so I won’t say anything.”
“What might that be, Lord Gaelion, the representative dragon of Shieldfreeden?”
Guh… Even the Queen is addressing Rival with the honorific “Lord”! This guy’s got his head in the clouds. Everyone, don’t be fooled!
“The Sword Hero is a level-grinding addict and a level-obsessed fanatic. Even if such a guy is hiding out, the ‘honey’ he’d produce should be in season right now in this country!”
The Queen nodded as if convinced by Rival’s proposal and hid her mouth with her fan. Ah, I see. Indeed, Ren would probably show up.
“It’s Cal Mira Island, isn’t it!”
“I see… revitalizing Cal Mira Island, huh… It certainly wouldn’t be surprising if the Hero were mingling among them.”
“Exactly. How about we bring in Naofumi and the others from Siltvelt to join us and boost our combat strength?”
“Wouldn’t it have been more efficient for us if Gaelion-chan had fought at sea?”
“That’s exactly why we need a small, elite force. If we use Cal Mira Island, we can boost our numbers significantly—even with the level cap.”
“…I see. Considering what lies ahead, it can’t hurt to go. It’s important, especially with the remnants of the Takt faction and such to consider.”
The representatives from Siltvelt, including the Queen, are nodding in agreement. This is a great opportunity. I’m going to buy up all the Filolial-sama and increase my numbers, too.
“And while we’re at it, Spear Hero. Since you’re the type who’s probably already thinking about increasing your Filolial-sama count anyway, this is the perfect chance.”
Dammit… that Rival of mine is throwing salt in my face again! Don’t read my mind!
“I’ll do it even without you telling me!”
“Now, now… Anyway, it’s a good spot to lure out Ren, who’s hiding somewhere and can’t be found.”
“Exactly. He might already be on the island.”
“Got it. Still… is it okay if I stay on the island and look for him?”
“Father, I’m here too, you know?”
For some reason, Father brushed me off.
“Motoyasu, you want to train more Filolials, don’t you? It’d be a problem if we had too many right now, but since it’s what you want to do, I suppose it’s fine.”
What?! So that suggestion was actually made with me in mind! But I need to be careful here.
“Rival, you’re planning to go after Father while I’m away, aren’t you?!”
Then, for some reason, Rival waved his hand sideways and acted like he was refusing.
“It’s a bit of a shame, but I have diplomatic engagements in Gaelion scheduled, so I won’t be able to join you until later.”
“Is something up?”

“Yeah. The Queen of Melromarc and the representative from Siltvelt—I’d like you to hear them out. The seal on the Spirit Tortoise is about to be broken soon. So, to minimize the number of victims, how about we engage in diplomacy with that country?”
Huh? So Rival isn’t coming to Cal Mira Island after all? This is a stroke of luck! A vacation on a southern island with Father and the others! Yippee! The hot sun and the blue sea are calling us!
“…You’re right. It might be a good idea to make a proposal in advance.”
“If it can reduce the casualties, there’s no reason not to do it.”
“Lord Gaelion, Representative of Shieldfreeden, are you aware of the time limit for the Spirit Tortoise’s seal?”
“Of course I am. If the heroes don’t get involved, I know exactly when the seal will be broken. I’d like to take care of this while the Sword Hero is still under the honey’s spell.”
It seems the discussion has progressed quite a bit.
“Do we have to participate?”
At this point, Father asks the Queen and Rival if he feels some sort of obligation. In response, the representatives all make grim faces and shake their heads.
“Honestly, we’d prefer to avoid sending the Heroes on a diplomatic mission to that country…”
“That country is arguably the most corrupt and exclusive of all. If the Heroes were to visit, who knows what they might do, taking advantage of the situation…”
“Unless it’s a matter the Heroes absolutely insist on handling, I think we should avoid it.”

Hmm… Was it really such a troubled country? Well, I did go in based on what I knew from the game at first. I headed straight for the Spirit Tortoise’s seal, which was my target. …Come to think of it, that was a foolish thing to do.
“So, leave it to Gaelion and the others!”
“Well, if Gaelion-chan says so… I guess it’ll be okay? What if we accidentally provoke the Spirit Tortoise into reviving, and the remaining Takt forces take advantage of the situation?”

“Hmm… That’s exactly why I want Naofumi and the others to get stronger. Gaelion should be able to hold off something like the Spirit Tortoise, so if the worst happens, I’d like them to come to our aid.”
“Hmm…”
Father is grumbling as if he’s troubled.
“Naofumi, do you think Gaelion is unreliable?”
It feels like Rival is seizing this opportunity to show off!
“It’s not exactly that, but…”
“Father! If anything happens, I’ll take care of it with ease!”
I won’t lose this time. Even if the Spirit Tortoise’s seal is broken and the Phoenix’s seal is broken, I’ll handle it swiftly this time.
“That’s right. In terms of combat power, as long as we have the Spear Hero, they’re no problem. Naofumi, I want you to be extra careful, though.”
He brushed it off casually. I get the feeling Rival’s evasion skills have improved. Rival from before would have argued back, but… I’ll have to be on my guard against this one.
“……I get it. But don’t take any unnecessary risks, okay?”
“Of course. When I think about how many lives could be lost because of a Gaelion mistake, I simply can’t afford to fail.”

And so, Rival has decided to lead a diplomatic mission to the country where the Spirit Tortoise is sealed. Not only the Queen, but the people of Siltvelt are going as well. Conversely, for once, Father and I are taking a different course of action.
My Assistant just sat there, staring intently at our exchange. Anyway, after discussing various other matters, the meeting seems to have concluded.

It appears Rival, the Queen, and the representatives from Siltvelt discussed the supplies and funds each country could allocate. It was all technical talk—a real hassle. For the most part, it seems we’re starting to break down the strongholds of the nobles who’ve amassed wealth thanks to our Rival’s rising approval ratings. While Shieldfreeden’s debt is enormous, things seem to be finally starting to turn around. All that’s left is to root out the remaining Takt forces and track down and confiscate the stolen national budget!

So, Father and I—though we’re not exactly thrilled about it—are here to keep an eye on Ren, who’s likely coming to Cal Mira Island at Rival’s suggestion. Since the portals on Cal Mira Island are out of commission during this time of year, we should at least be able to secure an opportunity to talk with Ren. Ren doesn’t harbor any hostility toward us, so it should be fine even if we run into him.
“Well then, Father, I’m going to go procure some of Filolial-sama’s eggs.”

“So that’s how it’s going to turn out, after all… Well, I’ll be making preparations for departure over in Siltvelt, so please don’t go overboard, Motoyasu-kun. After all, there are so many Filolials, and managing them is a real hassle.”
“Of course! First… let’s stop by and say hello to that Filolial breeder! I’ll bring Yuki-chan, Kou, and Sakura-chan along!”

Come to think of it, even though we’d bought some from them in this loop, we hadn’t gone to say hello. It’s time to show off Yuki-chan and the others, who’ve grown into legendary Filolials! So, I called out to Yuki-chan, Kou, and Sakura-chan, and we immediately used a portal to head over to the Filolial producer’s place.
“So we’re going to the place where Lord Motoyasu first acquired Yuki and the others, aren’t we?”
“That’s right.”
Before we set off, Yuki-chan asked me that, so I answered. It’s sort of like their birthplace. That breeder runs a great ranch.
“Hmm?”
“The place where you were when you were an egg?”
Sakura-chan and Kou don’t seem to get it.
“By the way, he’s a breeder who’s really dedicated to the Filolial Race. I think he’ll be someone Yuki-chan finds particularly interesting.”
“…I’m looking forward to it.”

Well, I already know he’ll end up causing trouble in the future world, so it’s pretty much stuck in my head. If I told them right now that Yuki is the ranch owner who’s been the talk of Shieldfreeden, I guarantee they’d be shocked.
“Alright, let’s go!”
“Ooh!”
We used a portal to teleport to Filolial Ranch. But what awaited us there was a sight beyond imagination.
“W-what is this—”
“W-what on earth is going on?! Filolial-samaaaaaaaaaaa!”

That’s right—all I could do was scream. The reason was that Filolial’s ranch area had been reduced to a scorched wasteland. The cozy, peaceful atmosphere of the ranch was gone… It had been reduced to scorched earth, with charred fences… and houses… Not a trace of tranquility remained in the area. Yuki-chan examines the charred fence.
“…It seems like this happened quite a while ago.”
I check it out too. Indeed… it’s completely cold to the touch. You can tell at a glance that it wasn’t burning just a moment ago. There’s no sign of smoke either. It looks like a complete ruin.
“W-what on earth is going on!?”
At least, nothing like this has ever happened in any of the loops so far. Could a Filolial producer have caused a fire by being careless with fire?

I’ll search the area. I check not only the Filolial shed where the producers were, but also the site of the warehouse where eggs and such were stored—but all that remains are the charred ruins. Hmm… I suppose I should ask around.
With that in mind, I’ll look for buildings nearby that seem to be associated with the Filolial industry. But… I’ve… found something.

Countless makeshift graves. And… the Monster Merchant and his companions, looking deeply sorrowful as they perform the burials. Yuki-chan and the others have sensed something ominous and are keeping their distance. I’ll have to ask them myself.
“Oh my, I believe that’s the Spear Hero over there. Yes.”
“H-hey, it’s been a while.”
“Yes… Thank you very much for patronizing our shop back then.”
“By the way, what are you doing here?”
“Well… we stopped by here to purchase monster eggs as part of our side business… but unfortunately, we’re not sure exactly what led to this situation. Yes.”
The monster merchant continues his explanation, seeming to struggle with the words.

“This entire area—whether it was bandits or monsters… we’re not sure exactly who—has been reduced to a scorched wasteland by an attack… and since the monsters’ corpses were left lying around, we’re in the middle of burying them.”

…… It seems the monster merchant is simply doing his job as a monster merchant. Since we ran into him in the middle of it, he’s burying the dead monsters. But… normally, monsters shouldn’t have a problem being left out in the open. So why does he have to bury them, I wonder?
